ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Establishing a Theoretical Framework for Shapley Value Computation
PROPOSAL: Derive non-asymptotic sample complexity bounds for randomized Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP and its variants. Specifically, use concentration inequalities to analyze the convergence rate of these estimators, leading to a trade-off between sample size and convergence rate.
CONTROLS: Prove that existing Shapley value computation methods, such as exact computation and local Erdos-Renyi estimation, are inefficient in terms of sample complexity by establishing lower bounds on the required sample size.
COST: 10650
PREDICTION: We expect to establish that KernelSHAP requires a sample size of at least O(d^2 * log(d)) to achieve a desired level of accuracy, and demonstrate the practical advantages of LeverageSHAP in high-dimensional settings. However, the efficiency of LeverageSHAP could be limited by the cost of computing statistical leverage scores, potentially leading to slower convergence rates in high-dimensional settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extension of Shapley Value Estimation to High-Dimensional Settings
PROPOSAL: Develop a new estimator, dubbed HyperSHAP, specifically designed for high-dimensional inputs. HyperSHAP leverages the desparsification technique to efficiently compute Shapley values in high-dimensional spaces by focusing on a subset of the most relevant features. We will then evaluate HyperSHAP in conjunction with existing methods on real-world datasets, such as ImageNet and Google's Like, Comment, Share dataset, to assess its performance in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of HyperSHAP to existing estimators, such as KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and SimSHAP, under different metrics (e.g., prediction accuracy, feature attribution quality, and computational efficiency). Also, analyze the properties of high-dimensional Shapley values that HyperSHAP can efficiently compute and display.
COST: 25800
PREDICTION: While HyperSHAP improves upon other estimators in high-dimensional settings, it might struggle with lower-dimensional inputs due to its focused feature selection approach. Additionally, its improved performance might come at the cost of increased computational complexity, limiting its applicability in time-sensitive applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Analyze the asymptotic behavior of KernelSHAP as the sample size increases using the weak convergence framework. We will establish the sufficient and necessary conditions for KernelSHAP to converge to the true Shapley values. This convergence analysis will enable a better understanding of the large-sample behavior of KernelSHAP and its limitations in various scenarios.
CONTROLS: Derive a set of sufficient conditions on the sampling distribution and the regularization parameter that guarantee asymptotic convergence. Compare these conditions with those required for LeverageSHAP to assess their relative strengths and weaknesses. Investigate potential outliers or pathological cases where KernelSHAP fails to converge.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect to show that KernelSHAP converges to the true Shapley values at a rate of O(1 / sqrt(n)), where n is the sample size. However, certain configurations or scenarios may lead to suboptimal convergence, which could impact the applicability and trustworthiness of KernelSHAP in practice.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of KernelSHAP with Variance Bound
PROPOSAL: Extend the asymptotic convergence analysis of KernelSHAP to establish a variance bound, enabling the estimation of confidence intervals around the Shapley value estimates. We will apply concentration inequalities to upper bound the variance of the estimator and derive a non-asymptotic error bound. This will allow for a more comprehensive understanding of the finite-sample properties of KernelSHAP and facilitate its use in production settings.
CONTROLS: Derived from the revised analysis, conduct experiments to demonstrate the practical value of the variance bound and assess its impact on the model's trustworthiness and reliability.
COST: 23400
PREDICTION: With the variance bound in place, we expect to observe a reduction in the mean-squared error (MSE) of the Shapley value estimates and an improvement in the overall accuracy of KernelSHAP, especially in scenarios with high-dimensional inputs or noisy data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Sampling for KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: Design an adaptive sampling mechanism for KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, leveraging the observed variances and statistical leverage scores to iteratively select the most informative samples. By utilizing this adaptive sampling approach, we aim to accelerate the convergence of both estimators while minimizing the required sample size. This can lead to significant computational savings, especially for large-scale datasets.
CONTROLS: Develop a non-asymptotic analysis to demonstrate the efficiency of the adaptive sampling approach and derive theoretical guarantees for the accelerated convergence of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. Investigate scenarios where adaptive sampling provides the most significant benefits and evaluate its practical impact on real-world datasets.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: With adaptive sampling, we anticipate a substantial reduction in the sample size required to achieve the same level of accuracy, potentially leading to orders-of-magnitude reductions in computational costs. However, the adaptive sampling mechanism may require additional resources to monitor and adjust the sampling process, potentially offsetting some of the benefits.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Extension of Shapley Value Estimation to High-Dimensional Settings with HyperSHAP
PROPOSAL: Enhance the descriptor-based HyperSHAP estimator to leverage learned representations from pre-trained neural networks, such as Word2Vec or BERT, to efficiently compute Shapley values in high-dimensional feature spaces. This hybrid approach combines the strengths of HyperSHAP's sparse feature selection with the expressive power of learned representations. We will conduct experiments on real-world datasets to evaluate the performance of this enhanced HyperSHAP in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: Investigate the impact of leveraging different types of learned representations (e.g., word embeddings, sentence embeddings, or image embeddings) on the accuracy and computational efficiency of HyperSHAP. Compare the performance of this enhanced HyperSHAP with state-of-the-art Shapley value estimators, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, on various datasets.
COST: 52920
PREDICTION: By integrating learned representations into HyperSHAP, we expect to observe improved accuracy and reduced computational costs, making it more suitable for high-dimensional feature spaces. However, this may come at the cost of increased overhead in terms of model pretraining and representation learning, which could impact the overall efficiency of the approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Computation of Shapley Values using Approximate Message Passing (AMP)
PROPOSAL: Apply Approximate Message Passing (AMP) to develop an efficient algorithm for computing Shapley values. AMP is a family of iterative algorithms that are particularly effective for solving certain types of linear systems and can be adapted for computing Shapley values by leveraging the underlying sparse structure. We will analyze the convergence properties of this AMP-based approach and evaluate its performance on real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Derive theoretical bounds on the convergence rate of the AMP algorithm and demonstrate its efficiency by comparing its computational costs with existing Shapley value estimators. Investigate scenarios where the AMP algorithm outperforms other methods and assess its sensitivity to parameter settings.
COST: 63480
PREDICTION: By leveraging the AMP algorithm, we expect to obtain a significant reduction in computational costs and potentially achieve real-time Shapley value computation on large-scale datasets. However, the convergence properties of AMP may be sensitive to the choice of parameters, requiring careful tuning to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Multi-Fidelity Approach to Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a multi-fidelity framework for Shapley value estimation, where a combination of low-fidelity and high-fidelity estimators is used to achieve improved accuracy and efficiency. The low-fidelity estimator provides a coarse approximation of the Shapley values, while the high-fidelity estimator refines the estimate using additional computations. We will design a Bayesian optimization approach to adaptively select the fidelity levels and trade off between accuracy and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Analyze the convergence properties of the multi-fidelity approach and derive bounds on its expected accuracy. Evaluate its performance on real-world datasets and compare it with existing Shapley value estimators. Investigate scenarios where the multi-fidelity approach provides significant benefits over other methods.
COST: 75000
PREDICTION: By leveraging the multi-fidelity approach, we expect to achieve improved accuracy and efficiency, particularly in scenarios where high-fidelity estimators are computationally expensive or have limited resources. However, the optimal choice of fidelity levels and trade-off between accuracy and computational cost may require careful tuning and experimentations.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Establishing a Theoretical Framework for Shapley Value Computation with Improved Convergence Rates
PROPOSAL: Strengthen the theoretical foundation of Shapley value computation by deriving improved convergence rates for existing estimators, such as KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. This involves refining the analysis of the underlying algorithms and leveraging advanced concentration inequalities to obtain tighter bounds on the estimation errors. The resulting theoretical framework will provide a more accurate understanding of the computational complexities and trade-offs involved in Shapley value estimation.
CONTROLS: Derive improved convergence rates for KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP by leveraging advances in probability theory and concentration inequalities. Evaluate the impact of these improved convergence rates on the computational costs and accuracy of Shapley value estimation. Compare the results with existing theoretical guarantees and experimental evaluations.
COST: 95000
PREDICTION: By establishing an improved theoretical framework, we expect to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the computational trade-offs involved in Shapley value estimation. This will enable the development of more efficient estimators and better choices of algorithmic parameters, ultimately leading to improved accuracy and reduced computational costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Shapley Value Estimation and Model Explanability
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework that integrates Shapley value estimation with model explainability, providing a comprehensive understanding of how model predictions are made and which features contribute to the prediction. This framework will leverage advanced techniques from explainability, such as feature importance and value sensitivity, to provide a more robust and interpretable understanding of models.
CONTROLS: Implement the unified framework on several case studies, including regression, classification, and neural networks, and evaluate its performance on various real-world datasets. Compare the results with existing explanation methods and Shapley value estimators.
COST: 105000
PREDICTION: By developing a unified framework, we expect to provide a more comprehensive understanding of model predictions and feature contributions, enabling improved model interpretability and trustworthiness. This will be particularly beneficial in high-stakes applications, such as medicine and finance, where model reliability and transparency are crucial.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Fusion Transformers for Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Train a state-of-the-art Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) for the task of temporal change description, conditioning on a sequence of satellite images, and evaluating using a combination of CIDEr, SPICE, and METEOR metrics.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing temporal change description methods (e.g. T-RNN, L-TABNET) and a strong vision-language transformer baseline (e.g. CLIP).
COST: 15120
PREDICTION: TFT will outperform existing methods and provide a robust understanding of the key dynamic changes over the observation period; potential failure: over-emphasis on recent events might lead to overlook early, yet critical, differences.

_extend this experimental TFT architecture with satellite-specific attention mechanisms to better fuse globally dispersed but temporally consistent information._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Satellite Conditioned Video Forecasting for Future Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Develop a variant of the popular Wav2VideoLeonardo (W2VL) model, conditioned on a sequence of pre-processed satellite images and their corresponding metadata (e.g. acquisition dates, orbital parameters), and evaluate its performance on future satellite image forecasting task, using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM).
CONTROLS: Compare with standard W2VL and a satellite-image conditioned DTW-GAN baseline, and ablate the satellite conditioning layer to check its effectiveness.
COST: 202400
PREDICTION: The satellite conditioned W2VL model will exhibit better temporal coherence and consistency in its forecasted images than the baseline models, potentially leading to more accurate and realistic-looking future satellite images; potential failure: distortion introduced by image pre-processing could reduce the model's overall quality.

_Extend the W2VL model to incorporate knowledge distillation from a pre-trained Temporal Change Description model (e.g. TFT in proposal 1) to leverage its understanding of the historical changes in the scene._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning for Long-Range Temporal Dynamics
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework for semantic-specific temporal reasoning, focusing on identifying abstract temporal patterns in long-range temporal dynamics; propose a proof technique based on encoding temporal dynamics into attributed relational graphs (ARGs) and reasoning about them using natural language processing-inspired meta-learning methods.
CONTROLS: Proof theoretical soundness by derivation, evaluate using abduction or entailment-based metrics on a novel synthetic dataset with explicitly annotated temporal dynamics.
COST: 477
PREDICTION: The semantic-specific temporal reasoning framework will provide an improved understanding of long-range temporal dynamics and temporal patterns, enabling better performance in temporal change description tasks; potential failure: the inductive bias of the ARG representation could be too restrictive, hindering model adaptation.

_Generate an experimental Semantics-specific Temporal Transformers (STT) model that incorporates the semantic-specific temporal reasoning framework into an existing temporal transformer architecture (e.g., T- Transformer), to boost the model's ability to capture complex, coherent long-range temporal patterns._

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning for Long-Range Temporal Dynamics
PROPOSAL: Refine the semantic-specific temporal reasoning framework by integrating attention-based graph neural networks (AGNNs) to selectively weigh the importance of different nodes and edges in the ARG representation, allowing for more nuanced reasoning about the encoded temporal dynamics; also incorporate temporal dependency awareness into the AGNN-based weights estimation process.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original semantic-specific temporal reasoning framework and the STT model, and assess how the addition of AGNN affects the model's ability to capture complex, coherent long-range temporal patterns.
COST: 2560
PREDICTION: The enhanced semantic-specific temporal reasoning framework will lead to significant improvements in temporal change description performance, particularly in scenes with complex and changing land-use patterns; potential failure: the attention-based weights estimation process might overlook long-range temporal dependencies.

_Integrate the Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning framework into the TFT model (Proposal 1) as an auxiliary reasoning module, allowing the TFT model to provide a deeper understanding of the historical changes described in the temporal change description output._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Forecasting via Discrete Latent Space Diffusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel image synthesis framework based on discrete latent space diffusion models, which encodes temporal consistency by broadcasting the forecasted changes in the discrete latent space to generate a temporally coherent and consistent forecasted image; evaluate the model using metrics such as Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and Temporal Coherence Score (TCS).
CONTROLS: Compare with existing diffusion-based image synthesis models and the Satellite Conditioned W2VL model (Proposal 2); also evaluate the effect of different discrete latent space configurations on temporal coherence.
COST: 2592
PREDICTION: The Temporally Consistent Forecasting via Discrete Latent Space Diffusion model will produce forecasts with high temporal coherence, effectively capturing the progression of changes observed in the historical sequence; potential failure: the model's performance might degrade in scenes with abrupt changes or outliers.

_Extend the Temporally Consistent Forecasting via Discrete Latent Space Diffusion model to incorporate a learned temporal weighting scheme, which assigns different importance weights to historical images based on the model's understanding of long-range temporal dynamics, as provided by the Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning framework (Proposal 3)._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Temporal Scale Cross-Attention for Long-Range Temporal Dynamics
PROPOSAL: Design a novel cross-attention mechanism that enables the interaction of different temporal scales within a single model, allowing for more effective long-range temporal reasoning and better capture of complex temporal patterns; integrate this mechanism into a variant of the T-Transformer model.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the effectiveness of the multi-temporal scale cross-attention mechanism by comparing the performance of the enhanced T-Transformer model with a standard T-Transformer baseline, as well as with other state-of-the-art temporal change description methods.
COST: 3029.6
PREDICTION: The multi-temporal scale cross-attention mechanism will lead to a significant improvement in the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns and long-range temporal dynamics, resulting in more accurate temporal change descriptions; potential failure: the increased computational cost of the cross-attention mechanism might become a bottleneck.

_Interface the Multi-Temporal Scale Cross-Attention Mechanism with the Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning framework (Proposal 3) and the Temporally Consistent Forecasting via Discrete Latent Space Diffusion model (Proposal 4) to create a comprehensive model architecture that can robustly handle long-range temporal dynamics._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Coherence Contrasted with Perceptual Quality (TCCPQ): A Novel Metric for Evaluating Temporal Consistency
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel evaluation metric, Temporal Coherence Contrasted with Perceptual Quality (TCCPQ), which combines the strengths of existing metrics for temporal coherence (e.g. TCS) and perceptual quality (e.g. PSNR, SSIM) to provide a comprehensive assessment of a forecast's temporal consistency and aesthetic appeal; validate TCCPQ using a set of diverse satellite image time series.
CONTROLS: Compare TCCPQ with a set of baseline metrics, including PSNR, SSIM, and TCS, and evaluate its ability to distinguish between forecasts with high temporal coherence but low perceptual quality, and vice versa.
COST: 10816
PREDICTION: The TCCPQ metric will provide a more nuanced understanding of a forecast's quality, allowing for better evaluation and optimization of models for satellite image time series forecasting; potential failure: the metric might be sensitive to specific characteristics of the dataset or application domain.

_Integrate the TCCPQ metric into the evaluation protocol for the Temporally Consistent Forecasting via Discrete Latent Space Diffusion model (Proposal 4), the Satellite Conditioned Video Forecasting for Future Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting (Proposal 2), and other models in the set, to provide a more comprehensive assessment of their performance._

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Hyper-Temporal Fusion Transformers for Multi-Temporal Scale Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: Revise the Temporal Fusion Transformers (TFT) model to incorporate a hyper-temporal fusion module, which enables the integration of multiple temporal scales within a single model, allowing for more effective long-range temporal reasoning and better capture of complex temporal patterns; integrate this module into the TFT architecture and train the model on a dataset with multiple temporal scales (e.g. hourly, daily, weekly satellite image time series).
CONTROLS: Evaluate the effectiveness of the hyper-temporal fusion module by comparing the performance of the revised TFT model with a standard TFT baseline, as well as with other state-of-the-art temporal change description methods.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: The hyper-temporal fusion module will lead to a significant improvement in the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns and long-range temporal dynamics, resulting in more accurate temporal change descriptions; potential failure: the increased computational cost of the hyper-temporal fusion module might become a bottleneck.

_Interface the revised Hyper-Temporal Fusion Transformers with the Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning framework (Proposal 3), the Multi-Temporal Scale Cross-Attention Mechanism (Proposal 5), and the TCCPQ metric (Proposal 6) to create a comprehensive model architecture that can robustly handle long-range temporal dynamics and provide a more nuanced understanding of a forecast's quality._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Change Description and Forecasting via Multi-Task Learning with Domain-Invariant Representation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a multi-task learning framework that jointly trains a model to perform both temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting tasks, with the goal of leveraging the understanding of past changes to inform the forecast; use a domain-invariant representation learning approach to ensure that the model learns a representation that is common across both tasks and robust to changes in the input data distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the multi-task learning model with a set of baseline models that are trained separately for each task, and evaluate the effectiveness of the domain-invariant representation learning approach.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: The multi-task learning model will lead to significant improvements in both temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting tasks, as well as enable better transfer of knowledge between the two tasks; potential failure: the model might overfit to the training data due to the increased complexity of the multi-task learning setting.

_Interface the multi-task learning framework with the revised Hyper-Temporal Fusion Transformers (Proposal 8), the Enhanced Semantic-Specific Temporal Reasoning framework (Proposal 3), the Multi-Temporal Scale Cross-Attention Mechanism (Proposal 5), and the TCCPQ metric (Proposal 6) to create a comprehensive model architecture that can robustly handle long-range temporal dynamics and provide a more nuanced understanding of a forecast's quality._

ACTION: REVISE 7
TITLE: Hyper-Temporal Fusion Transformers for Multi-Temporal Scale Temporal Change Description and Forecasting via Multi-Task Learning with Domain-Invariant Representation
PROPOSAL: Integrate the revised Hyper-Temporal Fusion Transformers (Proposal 8) and the multi-task learning framework with domain-invariant representation learning (Proposal 9) for a comprehensive model architecture that jointly trains a model to perform both temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting tasks, with the goal of leveraging the understanding of past changes to inform the forecast; use the hyper-temporal fusion module to enable the integration of multiple temporal scales within a single model, allowing for more effective long-range temporal reasoning and better capture of complex temporal patterns.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the comprehensive model architecture with a set of baseline models that are trained separately for each task, and evaluate the effectiveness of the domain-invariant representation learning approach and the hyper-temporal fusion module.
COST: 38880
PREDICTION: The comprehensive model architecture will lead to significant improvements in both temporal change description and future satellite image forecasting tasks, as well as enable better transfer of knowledge between the two tasks; potential failure: the model might overfit to the training data due to the increased complexity of the multi-task learning setting.

_This comprehensive model architecture will serve as the final solution to the research problem of understanding and forecasting change in satellite image time series._

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Online Learning for Time Series Forecasting using Ensemble Weights
PROPOSAL: Investigate online meta-learning methods that adapt the ensemble weights of pre-trained forecasting models to adjust to changing data distributions, using a combination of gradient-based updates and restarts from better-performing ensembles.
CONTROLS: Comparison with ("naive" online Ensemble Averaging, RI-Thomas tuning); ablation study on the importance of restarts vs gradient updates.
COST: 9,600
PREDICTION: Significant improvements in forecast accuracy online, especially when facing concept drift; potential failure: insensitivity of ensemble weights to changes in the underlying data distribution.

This experiment leverages the ensemble weights of pre-trained forecasting models, allowing the weights to adapt online to the changing data distribution. The combination of gradient-based updates and restarts from better-performing ensembles aims to balance exploration-exploitation trade-offs and improve forecasting accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adaptation Target on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate various update strategies targeting different components of pre-trained forecasting models, such as final layer weights, low-rank scaling coefficients, and adapters on the model's input or output, and analyze their impact on forecast accuracy and stability under various scenarios of distribution shift.
CONTROLS: Ablation studies targeting each adaptation component in isolation; comparison with vanilla OGD.
COST: 16,800
PREDICTION: The results will reveal the relative effectiveness of different adaptation targets under different scenarios of distribution shift, and potentially identify a subset of these targets that are more robust to concept drift and covariate shift.

This experiment aims to answer the question of which parameters to update, and how different adaptation targets affect the performance of online time series forecasting models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability and Accuracy Trade-offs in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate and quantify the trade-offs between stability (measured using metrics such as variance or stability metrics from literature) and forecast accuracy (measured using standard time series forecasting metrics) for various online adaptation strategies, and analyze how these trade-offs vary under different scenarios of distribution shift.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed trade-off metrics across different adaptation strategies; analytical analysis of the factors contributing to these trade-offs.
COST: 18,015
PREDICTION: The results will provide insights into the stability-accuracy trade-offs of online time series forecasting, highlighting the optimal adaptation strategies in different scenarios of distribution shift, and bring to light potential pitfalls of overly aggressive adaptation.

This experiment aims to provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental trade-offs in online time series forecasting, highlighting the tension between maintaining accurate forecasts and avoiding instability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Small-Batch Experience Replay Strategy for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate an experience replay strategy that stores and replays a small batch of recent observations to stabilize online gradient descent, focusing on minimizing the bias-variance trade-off and adapting to changing data distributions.
CONTROLS: Ablation study on the batch size and the role of recent vs older samples; comparison with standard experience replay.
COST: 19,200
PREDICTION: The results will demonstrate the benefits of a tuned experience replay strategy, significantly improving the stability and accuracy of online time series forecasting models, especially when facing concept drift and covariate shift.

This experiment leverages experience replay to improve the stability and accuracy of online time series forecasting, adapting to changing data distributions and maintaining the balance between exploration and exploitation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Normalization-based Covariate Shift Mitigation for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a normalization-based approach to mitigate covariate shift in online time series forecasting, normalizing the input data at each time step based on learned statistics, and analyze its impact on forecast accuracy and robustness to distribution shift.
CONTROLS: Comparison with standard normalization methods and a naive baseline; ablation study on the impact of statistics learning.
COST: 23,040
PREDICTION: The results will show improved forecast accuracy and robustness to covariate shift when using normalization-based covariate shift mitigation, especially under scenarios with significant changes in the input distribution.

This experiment explores normalization-based methods as an effective and efficient way to adapt to changing input distributions, ensuring that the model is trained with normalized data, and showing its benefits in online time series forecasting applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Multi-Step Time Series Forecasting using Delay Compensated Unlearning
PROPOSAL: Propose and evaluate an online multi-step time series forecasting approach that uses a delay-compensated unlearning mechanism to adjust the model updates, considering the delayed feedback in multi-step forecasting and the impact of unlearning on model stability.
CONTROLS: Ablation study on the effect of different unlearning rates and mechanism variations; comparison with standard online multi-step methods.
COST: 26,878.7
PREDICTION: The results will show improved accuracy and stability of online multi-step time series forecasting, especially under scenarios with concept drift and delayed feedback.

This experiment addresses the challenges of multi-step time series forecasting by proposing an innovative approach that combines unlearning and delay compensation, enabling the model to adapt to evolving patterns more effectively and accurately.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Empirical Analysis of Distribution Shift Detection Methods for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare state-of-the-art distribution shift detection methods to analyze their effectiveness in identifying concept drift and covariate shift in online time series forecasting, and evaluate their impact on adaptation strategies.
CONTROLS: Ablation study on the detection methods and adaptation strategies; comparison with naive baselines.
COST: 28,000
PREDICTION: The results will provide insights into the performance and limitations of various distribution shift detection methods and inform the development of effective adaptation strategies for online time series forecasting.

This experiment aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the current state of distribution shift detection methods, evaluating their ability to accurately identify concept drift and covariate shift in online time series forecasting applications, and examining their interaction with adaptation strategies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time Series Forecasting with Online Attention: Adaptation to Concept Drift and Covariate Shift
PROPOSAL: Propose an online attention mechanism for time series forecasting that adaptively focuses on the most relevant features and updates the model online to address concept drift and covariate shift.
CONTROLS: Evaluation of the attention mechanism on traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and other real-world time series datasets; ablation study on the effect of different attention mechanisms and update strategies.
COST: 30,480
PREDICTION: The results will demonstrate the effectiveness of online attention in improving time series forecasting accuracy and adaptability under scenarios with concept drift and covariate shift.

This experiment leverages the power of online attention mechanisms to selectively focus on the most relevant features for time series forecasting, enabling the model to adapt more flexibly to changing patterns and distributions.

TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret for Online Time Series Forecasting with Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Derive and analyze the dynamic regret bounds for online time series forecasting with widespread adaptation methods, providing a theoretical understanding of the trade-offs between exploration and exploitation in online adaptation.
CONTROLS: Derive the regret bounds for different adaptation strategies (e.g., adaptive online learning, experience replay, online attention); comparison with the oracle regret bound.
COST: 32,512
PREDICTION: The results will provide theoretical insights into the performance of online time series forecasting methods with adaptation, highlighting the importance of balancing exploration and exploitation in online adaptation.

This experiment aims to provide a theoretical foundation for understanding the dynamic regret of online time series forecasting methods with adaptation, providing a framework for analyzing and comparing the performance of different adaptation strategies.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Online Time Series Forecasting: An Empirical and Theoretical Exploration
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of meta-learning for online time series forecasting, proposing a novel approach that combines meta-learning with adaptation strategies and theoretical analysis to improve the performance of online time series forecasting under concept drift and covariate shift.
CONTROLS: Empirical evaluation of the proposed approach on real-world time series datasets; ablation study on the effect of different meta-learning architectures and adaptation strategies; comparison with state-of-the-art online time series forecasting methods.
COST: 40,000
PREDICTION: The results will demonstrate the potential of meta-learning for online time series forecasting, improving the adaptability and accuracy of the model under scenarios with concept drift and covariate shift.

This experiment aims to provide a comprehensive exploration of meta-learning for online time series forecasting, combining empirical and theoretical analysis to propose a novel approach that leverages the strengths of meta-learning and adaptation strategies to improve the performance of online time series forecasting.

PROPOSAL: We will propose a novel unsupervised anomaly detection approach for univariate time series, building upon the concept of adversarial autoencoders. The model consists of two components: an encoder that maps the input time series to a lower-dimensional latent space and a decoder that reconstructs the original time series from this latent representation. The encoder and decoder are matched in their ability to reconstruct normal times series, while the discriminator is matched in its ability to correctly classify normal and anomalous times series.
